title: Russia Just Launched 656 Drones and 73 Missiles at Ukraine in a Single Night. At Least 11 Are Dead.
excerpt: The assault on Kyiv, Dnipro, and Kharkiv included eight Zircon hypersonic missiles — the largest single use of the weapon in the war. Poland scrambled jets. Oil climbed again. India stayed silent.
body:
Russia unleashed one of the deadliest aerial bombardments of its four-year war against Ukraine overnight on Tuesday, killing at least 11 people and wounding more than 100 across the country. The strikes targeted residential buildings, kindergartens, and apartment blocks in Kyiv, Dnipro, Kharkiv, and Zaporizhzhia.

Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 656 drones and 73 missiles in the overnight barrage. Ukrainian defences intercepted 40 missiles and 602 drones, but the sheer volume overwhelmed air defence systems in multiple cities. A suspected missile strike caused a 24-storey apartment building in Kyiv's Podilsky district to partially collapse, with people feared trapped under the rubble.

The Zircon Factor

The attack included eight Zircon hypersonic missiles — likely the largest single deployment of the weapon since Russia began using it in combat. The Zircon has a range of 1,000 km and travels at nine times the speed of sound, making it nearly impossible to intercept with conventional air defence systems. Ukraine relies heavily on Patriot systems to counter ballistic threats, but a global shortage of Patriot interceptor missiles has left gaps in coverage.

Russia's defence ministry said it had carried out a "massive strike" on Ukraine's defence industry facilities using "high-precision long-range weapons." But the destruction of residential buildings, burnt-out cars, and a damaged children's playground in Dnipro told a different story.

What Triggered the Escalation

The Kremlin had warned last week of "systematic strikes" on Kyiv targets in response to a Ukrainian drone attack on a dormitory in the Russian-held Luhansk region that killed 21 people. Ukraine denied responsibility for that strike. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy had warned on Monday evening that intelligence indicated a massive Russian assault was imminent.

"Intelligence warnings regarding Russian strikes remain in effect. A massive strike is possible. They have prepared one," Zelenskiy said in his nightly address, hours before the barrage began.

The Scene in Kyiv

Thousands of residents flooded into Kyiv's metro system before dawn, carrying pets, mattresses, and belongings as explosions echoed above ground. Mayor Vitali Klitschko described the overnight assault as a "massive enemy attack" and reported fires in multiple districts.

"We couldn't understand what was happening — some kind of apocalypse?" said Olha Mudra, standing at the site of one strike with her six-year-old daughter Natalia, surrounded by destroyed buildings and smoke.

In Dnipro, six people were killed and 36 injured, including a rescue worker killed in a "double-tap" strike — a tactic where a second missile targets first responders who arrive at the scene of an initial attack. A child was among the 10 injured in Kharkiv.

NATO and Global Response

Poland scrambled military jets to secure its airspace after the strikes, a reminder of how close the war's violence reaches to NATO territory. EU and NATO members have repeatedly warned that Russian strikes near the Polish border risk dragging the alliance into direct confrontation.

Why It Matters for India

The escalation carries direct economic consequences for India. Oil prices rose 4% on Monday and continued climbing Tuesday as the broader geopolitical picture — the Iran-US standoff, the Hormuz blockade, and now intensified fighting in Ukraine — compressed global energy supply.

India imports over 80% of its crude oil, and Brent crude near $93 per barrel is already straining the current account. The rupee has weakened to ₹95 against the dollar, and the Reserve Bank of India faces its monetary policy decision on Friday against this volatile backdrop.

India has maintained a carefully neutral stance on the Russia-Ukraine war, abstaining from UN votes condemning the invasion while continuing to buy discounted Russian crude. But each escalation tests that position. An estimated 18,000 Indian students were evacuated from Ukraine in 2022 under Operation Ganga, and thousands more have since relocated to medical colleges across Central Asia.

New Delhi has not yet issued a formal statement on Tuesday's attacks. India's standard position — calling for dialogue and diplomacy — has grown increasingly strained as the war's human toll mounts and its economic shockwaves reach Indian shores.

Sources: Reuters, CNN, Ukraine Air Force (Telegram), ISW assessment, S&P Global
author: Diaspora Desk
